newsitem.title: USA: Judge admits tobacco industry booklet at Fla. trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge admits tobacco industry booklet at Fla. trial.

text.p: A 1974 tobacco industry publication that concluded there was no definitive proof cigarette smoking caused cancer was entered into evidence Friday at the trial of a wrongful death lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.

Judge Bernard Nachman allowed the booklet, titled "The Cigarette Controversy" and written by The Tobacco Institute, an industry trade group, into evidence over the objections of Reynolds' lawyers, who said it was irrelevant.
In admitting the booklet into evidence, however, the judge said it could be used by the jury only to consider punitive damages.
Plaintiff Dana Raulerson sued the tobacco company on behalf of the estate and children of her sister, Jean Connor, who smoked heavily and died of lung cancer in 1995 at age 49.

The booklet posed the question "Does it (smoking) cause illness -- even death?" and provided the answer "No one knows." It concluded that there was no definitive scientific research proving smoking caused cancer.
The booklet appeared to contradict a Reynolds internal company document already entered as evidence in the trial.
The 1962 document, written by Alan Rodgman, a senior researcher at the tobacco company, said "the amount of evidence accumulated to indict cigarette smoking as a health hazard is overwhelming."

A key facet of Raulerson's lawsuit against Reynolds is the claim that Reynolds executives knew decades ago that cigarette smoking was a health hazard and that they were selling a dangerous product, but failed to warn the public or to fix it.
On Thursday a plaintiff's witness, Dr. Victor Roggli, a Duke University forensic pathologist, testified that he was virtually certain Jean Connor died of lung cancer caused by smoking.
Roggli, on the stand again Friday, said the booklet's claim that no one knew whether smoking was a health hazard was untrue.
Lawyers said Raulerson could take the witness stand later Friday.
The plaintiffs were expected to wrap up their case by the middle of next week.
R.J. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
